localChanges: When the defender of a stack outside a city loses, every unit in the stack is now destroyed, as in Civ1 (closes #70).
If one of a computer player's units hits a problem while moving, only that unit waits for the turn; the rest of their units still move (#79).

log: LandAircraft extends Move. After the move it empties the aircraft's moves and sets it inactive, because landing ends its turn. Given a transport (a Carrier), it also stows the aircraft aboard and marks it with Embark's Stowed busy rule, then re-processes Moved as Embark does. Without a transport (a city) nothing is stowed.

It is named LandAircraft rather than Land so it doesn't clash with the Land unit and terrain types in the ClassRegistry, DataObject ids and the data transfer's action names (civ-clone/web-renderer#81).

`civ1-unit:unit/defeated/destroy-stack` processed `Destroyed` for the defender once per stack mate instead of for each stack mate, so the rest of the stack survived. It now filters the stack first, which also avoids iterating the registry's result while units are destroyed, and destroys each of the defender's own units on the tile.
Adds tests/defeated.test.ts: a stack of three in open country is destroyed, in a city only the defender is, and another player's unit on the tile is untouched.

CI now uses the standard workflow (Node 22, pnpm without a lock file, `--if-present` scripts). `prettier:check` passes `--check`, so it fails on unformatted files instead of printing them. `Rules/Unit/action.ts` imports `@civ-clone/core-terrain-feature/TerrainFeatureRegistry`, which is now declared, so `tsc --build` no longer fails with TS2307 in a clean install.
chore: remove the stale yarn.lock now that CI installs with pnpm (civ-clone/web-renderer#66)

Adds civ1-unit:unit/action/land-aircraft, offering LandAircraft (from the new @civ-clone/base-unit-action-land-aircraft) when an Air unit moves onto one of its player's cities, or onto a friendly NavalTransport with capacity that canStow it. On a Carrier the aircraft is stowed and marked Stowed, so the fuel rule's transportRegistry.hasUnit check counts it as landed; in a city (also a city with a Carrier in it) it just lands. Either way its moves are emptied. The shared canLandAircraft check also removes those tiles from the Air branch of civ1-unit:unit/action/move, so LandAircraft is the only action there (civ-clone/web-renderer#81).

Taking off: Disembark sets moves to 0, which would strand a Fighter, so Air units no longer get Disembark. They take off with a plain Move, and the new civ1-unit:unit/moved/take-off rule unloads an Air unit (and clears Stowed) once it has left its transport's tile. The new civ1-unit:unit/movement-cost/transported/air rule makes the move-cargo Move free for an Air unit following its Carrier, since a landed aircraft has no moves left and would otherwise be left behind.

Each mandatory action in `takeTurn()` is now handled in its own try/catch. When handling a `Unit` throws (a rule failing inside `unit.action()` or `unit.actions()`), the error is logged with the unit's id, the unit is given `NoOrders` (or, if that throws too, has its moves zeroed and is set inactive) and the loop carries on with the player's other units. Errors from anything other than a unit still reject `takeTurn()` as before, since skipping a city build or research choice has no safe fallback.
Adds a regression test: a `Moved` rule that throws for one Warrior no longer stops a second Warrior from moving that turn.

CI now uses the standard workflow (Node 22, pnpm without a lock file, `--if-present` scripts). `prettier:check` passes `--check`, so it fails on unformatted files instead of printing them. `SimpleAIClient.ts` imports `@civ-clone/civ1-world` and `@civ-clone/core-unit-transport`, which are now declared, so a strict pnpm install resolves them without hoisting.
chore: core-unit-transport is only used by the tests, so it's a dev dependency
chore: remove the stale yarn.lock now that CI installs with pnpm (civ-clone/web-renderer#66)
